We investigate the propagation of a localized baryon number pulse through a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) using a holographic framework. This setup models a heavy ion collision where a baryon-rich fireball is created at mid-rapidity. We analyze the evolution of this pulse by solving the dynamics of a probe string within a black brane background, which represents the QGP. Our findings indicate that the baryon number pulse travels at a velocity exceeding the speed of sound.

This paper examines the Eberlein-Grothendieck property within the context of locally convex spaces consisting of continuous functions on a topological space $X$. We demonstrate that for a first-countable Tychonoff space $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ is Eberlein-Grothekieck if and only if $X$ is a locally compact $\sigma$-space. Furthermore, for any Tychonoff space $X$, the space $C(X)$ is Eberlein-Grothendieck precisely when $X$ is a locally compact scattered space.

This study examines the isochronicity problem for a specific class of Hamiltonian systems with a single degree of freedom. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for such a system to exhibit an isochronous center and derive the isomonodromic deformation equations associated with its linearization. Furthermore, we present a concrete example of a system that satisfies isomonodromic deformation.

This study examines the Lorenz system's behavior across a broad spectrum of parameters, specifically the Rayleigh number ($r$) and Prandtl number ($\sigma$). We introduce a novel approach to analyze the system's dynamics, utilizing the similarity signature curve (SSC) to track the evolution of the Lorenz attractor. This curve is defined by the ratio of the two non-trivial fixed points, $x_1$ and $x_2$, and serves as a reliable indicator of the attractor's symmetry. Our findings reveal that the SSC exhibits a distinctive "sawtooth" pattern, where the attractor's symmetry alternates between symmetric and asymmetric states. This pattern is observed in both the original Lorenz system and the extended version (Lorenz-96). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the SSC can effectively identify the transition from a symmetric to an asymmetric attractor, as well as the shift from a symmetric to a symmetric state.

This paper examines the LAN property within a parametric statistical framework. We establish the property for a specific class of models, which includes the classical normal model with unknown parameters and the normal model with unknown covariance matrix.
This paper demonstrates that for non self-adjoint Laplacians acting on flat vector bundles over compact hyperbolic surfaces, the spectrum adheres to Weyl's law.

This study introduces FNetAR, a new architecture for causal language modeling that eliminates recurrent components and self-attention mechanisms. Instead, it employs a novel attention mechanism that enables the model to capture long-range dependencies with minimal computational overhead. Our approach achieves performance comparable to Transformer-XL on the WikiText-103 benchmark while requiring only 1/10th of the parameters and 1/10th of the training time. Additionally, FNetAT demonstrates superior performance on the Penn Treebank and WikiText-103 datasets compared to the original FNet model.

This study examines the transition from cosmic deceleration to acceleration within the framework of $f(R,T)$ gravity, utilizing a time-dependent equation of state. The analysis focuses on the epoch when the universe's expansion rate shifts from slowing down to speeding up. The paper derives the specific form of the $f(R,T)$ Lagrangian required to model this transition and subsequently determines the corresponding Hubble parameter.

This paper introduces a game-theoretic approach to optimize Service Function Chaining (SFC) placement at the network edge, aiming to minimize the total cost of SFC providers. We model the interaction between SFC providers and a network operator as a non-cooperative game, where each provider seeks to reduce their own expenses by strategically selecting a subset of edge nodes for service placement. We demonstrate that the resulting game possesses a potential function, ensuring the existence of at least one Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, we propose a low-complexity algorithm to identify the optimal strategy for each provider. Simulation results indicate that our proposed method achieves a lower total cost for SFC providers compared to existing solutions.

We investigate the phase diagram of two-dimensional disordered superconductors, which exhibits a complex interplay between the diffusive thermal metal, topological superconductor, and superfluid phases. This system displays a phase transition between the diffusive thermal metal and topological superconductor, characterized by a diverging superfluid stiffness and a vanishing thermal Hall conductivity. This transition is driven by the emergence of a topological superconducting edge state, which is confirmed by the appearance of a quantized Hall conductance. This study provides a comprehensive understanding of the phase diagram and its implications for the development of new quantum materials.

This study examines the relationship between depression and the pursuit of happiness within Twitter data. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 10,000 tweets, each labeled for depression, happiness, or both. Our analysis reveals that depression is associated with a diminished interest in happiness, and we further demonstrate that incorporating happiness-related features enhances the performance of depression detection models.

This article provides a concise overview of the current status of dark matter research in astrophysics, along with a brief summary of theoretical dark matter candidates, including axions, WIMPs, and primordial black holes.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the magnetic properties of the spin-1 system Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$, which exhibits a unique magnetic phase diagram. By examining the temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and magnetization, we identified a Neel temperature of $T_N = 10.5$ K. Below this threshold, the Ni$^{2+}$ moments organize into a spiral structure with a propagation vector of $k = (0, 0.5, 0)$. Furthermore, we observed a spin reorientation transition at $T^* = 6.5$ K, where the spiral vector shifts from the $b^*$ direction to the $a^*$ direction. Theoretical modeling of the magnetic susceptibility using a spin spiral framework, combined with specific heat data, yielded the exchange interactions $J_1 = 1.0$ K, $J_2 = 0.1$ K, and $J_3 = 0.05$ K. Additionally, we measured the magnetization curve at 2 K, revealing a saturation moment of $0.8 \mu_B$ and a critical field of $H_c = 1.5$ T.

The increasing adoption of IoT networks has heightened the need for dependable and trustworthy data. However, the inherent uncertainty of data sources and the potential for malicious actors to compromise trustworthiness complicate the establishment of reliable data. This paper introduces a novel framework for assessing data trustworthiness within IoT environments, which integrates both the reliability of data sources and the trustworthiness of communication channels. The proposed approach employs a Bayesian network to model the propagation of uncertainty from sources through channels, ultimately quantifying the trustworthiness of the received data.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for resolving the Gibbs phenomenon in spline interpolation. We demonstrate that the Gibbs phenomenon can be effectively mitigated by employing a specific type of weighted average.

This study examines four-dimensional Taub-NUT spacetimes within Einstein-$\Lambda$ theory, focusing on the case where the cosmological constant is negative. We demonstrate that these spacetimes encompass both black hole and cosmological solutions, which can be derived from the Kerr-Newman-NUT-AdS metric by setting the electric and magnetic charges to zero. Furthermore, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the metric and the associated conserved charges, which are calculated using the counterterm formalism.

Accurate annotation is essential for Information Retrieval (IR) systems handling multimedia data. However, manually labeling such content is often costly and time-consuming. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that leverages a pre-trained language model to automatically generate captions for images. This method is evaluated on the MS-COCO dataset, where it demonstrates strong performance by producing captions that align well with human preferences.

The coexistence of numerous species within extensive ecosystems remains a fundamental mystery in ecology. While the classical theory of competitive exclusion posits that species with similar resource needs cannot survive together, recent research indicates that diversity is sustained by a combination of mechanisms, including niche partitioning, environmental fluctuations, and spatial heterogeneity. This study introduces a novel mechanism rooted in the non-linear dynamics of the underlying food web. We demonstrate that in a system comprising a single resource and multiple competing consumers, the presence of a shared predator can facilitate the coexistence of consumers that would otherwise be excluded. This phenomenon arises from the predator's ability to alter the effective competitive interactions among prey species.

This study examines the dynamics of cascading failures within networks, specifically focusing on the propagation of node removals triggered by an initial assault. We introduce a novel framework for analyzing this phenomenon, termed the "avaline," which is defined by the rapid, exponential decline in the count of surviving nodes. We demonstrate that this process can be modeled using a stochastic differential equation, which facilitates the calculation of the critical threshold for avalanche initiation. Furthermore, we derive an analytical formula for the total number of nodes eliminated during an avalanche, which is shown to be proportional to the square root of the initial network size.

This paper introduces a novel approach to text comprehension that prioritizes the generation of questions requiring multi-hop reasoning. We present a model that learns to produce inquiries demanding multi-hop reasoning by leveraging a question generation framework trained on a newly developed dataset. This dataset is constructed by synthesizing questions from the HotpotQA corpus, specifically targeting those that necessitate multi-hop reasoning. We evaluate our model's performance using a metric that assesses the depth of understanding demonstrated in generated questions, defined by the number of hops required to answer them. Our results indicate that our model successfully produces questions reflecting a deep understanding of the text, with a significant portion requiring multi-hop reasoning.

This study introduces a new finite element approach for solving the Helmholtz equation within a bounded domain, utilizing perfectly matched layers (PML) to handle the exterior region. The proposed method employs a conforming finite element framework for the interior domain, while applying a non-conforming scheme in the exterior. The analysis demonstrates the method's stability and establishes error estimates in the energy norm, contingent upon the PML thickness and the polynomial degree of the finite elements. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical findings.

This study examines the fluid dynamic response of a droplet array subjected to a sudden pressure impulse. We demonstrate that the resulting dynamics are governed by the dimensionless parameter $\mathcal{P}$, which represents the ratio of the impulse to the surface tension of a solitary droplet. By manipulating the impulse magnitude, droplet spacing, and surface tension, one can regulate the flow evolution. Specifically, the droplet array's behavior is categorized into three distinct regimes: (i) a single-jet regime, (ii) a multi-jet regime, and (iii) a multi-jet coalescence regime. In the single-jet scenario, a primary jet forms between each pair of droplets, whereas the multi-jet scenario involves the formation of multiple jets within the interstitial space. Furthermore, the multi-jet coalescence regime is characterized by the merging of these multiple jets.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, with billions of devices anticipated to be connected by 2025. These devices are increasingly integrated into critical sectors such as healthcare, transportation, and smart cities, where Quality of Service (QoS) is paramount. Consequently, there is a growing demand for network architectures capable of delivering high-speed, low-latency connectivity. Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers a promising solution by enabling dynamic, programmable network management. This paper introduces a novel, SDN-based architecture designed to ensure QoS for IoT applications. The proposed framework leverages OpenFlow rules to facilitate real-time traffic management and prioritization, thereby optimizing network performance.

This study presents ALMA observations of the protoplanetary disk surrounding the young star HD 169142, which exhibits a prominent gap. By analyzing the disk's structure and kinematics, we determined that the gap is likely carved by a planet with a mass of 1.5 to 2.5 Jupiter masses orbiting at a distance of 100 to 140 astronomical units. The disk's kinematics also reveal a significant asymmetry in the gas distribution, which we attribute to a companion star located approximately 1000 astronomical units away.

This study introduces a vector-valued distance metric for symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices, which is subsequently employed to formulate a novel generalized least squares (GLS) estimator. The proposed GLS estimator is derived by minimizing the vector-valued distance between the data and the model using the newly defined SPD distance metric. Theoretically, we demonstrate that this estimator possesses asymptotic normality and achieves a minimax lower bound. Furthermore, numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the estimator's performance against existing methods.

This study examines the potential of hydrogen networks to mitigate renewable energy supply fluctuations. By analyzing a simplified model of a hydrogen network, we demonstrate that it can effectively balance renewable variations. Furthermore, we show that a hydrogen network can be represented as a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) system, which facilitates the design of optimal control strategies.

This study introduces a novel technique for estimating the orientation of subsurface horizontal magnetic fields by analyzing travel time anisotropy in seismic data. The method utilizes a 3D ray tracing model to calculate the travel time of a ray traversing a horizontally stratified medium with a magnetic field oriented in a specific direction. The resulting travel time equation is expressed as a function of the ray's take-off angle, the magnetic field's orientation, and the ray's path length. By fitting this equation to observed travel time anisotropy, the magnetic field's orientation can be determined. The proposed approach is validated using synthetic data generated from a 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a solar active region. The estimated orientations align well with the true orientations, demonstrating that the method can accurately recover the magnetic field's direction from travel time anisotropy measurements.

Squeezed light is essential for advancing quantum information processing and sensing, yet generating it remains a significant challenge. We introduce a novel approach to produce squeezed light using a single-mode optical parametric oscillator (OPO) that incorporates a single-photon source. This setup utilizes a single-photon source to drive the OPO, which is then pumped by a laser. The single-photon source is realized through a quantum dot (QD) integrated with a photonic crystal nanocavity. The system is designed to operate in the OPO's squeezed regime, which is achieved by tuning the QD's emission frequency to match the OPO's resonance frequency. Theoretical analysis indicates that this configuration can generate squeezed light with a noise reduction of up to 10 dB.

This study addresses the challenge of controlling a drone to reach a target waypoint in the shortest possible time. We formulate the problem as a linear optimal control task and solve it using Pontryagin's minimum principle. The resulting optimal control input is derived as a piecewise constant function, with switching times determined by the solution to a quadratic equation. The paper also examines the impact of wind on the drone's trajectory and demonstrates that the optimal control strategy remains piecewise constant even under windy conditions.

This paper examines additive conjugacy codes defined over finite fields. We demonstrate that for any such code over these fields, an equivalent linear cyclic code exists over a specific subfield. Furthermore, we establish that the minimum distance of this resulting linear cyclic code does not exceed that of the original additive conjugacy code.

Physicists seeking employment at undergraduate-focused institutions and community colleges face a significant hurdle: the scarcity of existing, high-quality instructional materials tailored to these specific educational levels. This paper introduces a new resource designed to address this gap, featuring a comprehensive collection of problems and solutions for introductory courses in both calculus-based and algebra-based physics.

This study reports on the polarization of W bosons produced in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, utilizing the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The analysis focuses on the decay $W \rightarrow \ell\nu$, where $\ell$ represents either an electron or a muon. The polarization is determined by examining the angular distribution of the charged lepton within the W boson's rest frame. The dataset comprises 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The observed W boson polarization fractions for the longitudinal, left-handed, and right-handed states are measured as $f_{0} = 0.207 \pm 0.004$ (stat.) $\pm$ 0.004 (syst.), $f_{-} = 0.343 \pm 0.004$ (stat.) $\pm$ 0.004 (syst.), and $f_{+} = 0.450 \pm 0.004$ (stat.) $\pm$ 0.004 (syst.), respectively. These findings align with the Standard Model predictions.

This study examines the twist-2 and twist-3 D-meson distribution amplitudes within the framework of light-cone QCD sum rules. We derive the corresponding twist-2 and twist-3 D*-meson counterparts by applying the standard QCD sum rule methodology. These results are crucial for analyzing B-meson decays into D-mesons and light pseudoscalar mesons via the weak interaction.

This paper investigates the characteristic polynomials of power hypergraphs, with a specific focus on those derived from signed simple hypergraphs. We demonstrate that the eigenvalues of signed subgraphs within these structures are instrumental in producing the eigenvalues of their corresponding power counterparts. Furthermore, we establish a recurrence relation for the characteristic polynomials of signed power hypergraphs and derive the eigenvalues for several specific classes.

The growing number of satellites in mega-constellations is driving a surge in space traffic, which in turn increases the demand for precise satellite positioning. This paper investigates cooperative localization within such constellations, where satellites exchange position data to enhance their own and neighboring measurements. We propose a decentralized algorithm that leverages inter-satellite links to refine position estimates, thereby reducing the reliance on ground stations. The study evaluates the algorithm's performance using a realistic simulation of a low-Earth orbit constellation. Results indicate that this approach significantly improves positioning accuracy, particularly for satellites located far from ground stations.

We report the discovery of a second planet orbiting the star HD 160617, a system previously known to host a hot Jupiter. This new planet, designated HD 160617 b, was identified through transit timing variations (TTVs) in the primary planet's orbit, which were detected by analyzing the radial velocity data from the HARPS spectrograph. The system's architecture is defined by a hot Jupiter with a mass of 0.93 M$_{\rm Jup}$ and a period of 3.5 days, accompanied by a Neptune-mass companion with a period of 10.5 days. The two planets are in a 3:2 mean motion resonance, and the observed TTVs are consistent with a model of orbital migration driven by tidal dissipation within the host star.

This study introduces a novel calibration approach for the CMB-S4 experiment, leveraging the distinct characteristics of the telescope's optics. By utilizing the telescope's inherent symmetry, we can enhance both the sensitivity and precision of signal calibration. The methodology involves applying a specific filter to the data that isolates the contribution from the telescope's optics, thereby enabling the separation of the optics' signal from the actual sky signal. This separation is achieved through a Bayesian framework, which employs a Gaussian process to model the optics' signal and a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm to estimate the parameters of the Gaussian process. The approach is validated using simulated data from the CMB-S4 telescope, demonstrating that the method can accurately recover the optics' signal and its parameters.
We demonstrate that for an algebraic $G$KM manifold, any two equivariant vector bundles sharing identical equivariant Chern classes are necessarily isomorphic.
We present a novel proof of prime number theorem that relies on the analytic properties of the Riemann zeta function.

Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis is a prevalent method for analyzing clinical trials with repeated assessments. However, when the time variable is treated as categorical, the MMRM model relies on the assumption that the variance-covariance matrix remains constant across all time points. This assumption is frequently violated in practice, particularly in trials involving multiple assessments. In such cases, the time variable is often recorded as a continuous metric, and the MMRM model is applied using continuous time. This study evaluates the performance of MMRM models under both categorical and continuous time specifications, specifically focusing on scenarios where the variance-covariance matrix varies across time points. The findings indicate that the continuous time approach yields superior results compared to the categorical time approach when the latter's assumption of constant variance is violated.

This paper introduces a crowdsourcing-based algorithm designed to route connected vehicles. The method utilizes a fleet of connected vehicles to gather real-time traffic data, which is then transmitted to a central server. This server processes the information to generate traffic maps and subsequently directs vehicles along optimal paths. The proposed approach is evaluated against a baseline routing strategy that relies solely on historical data. The findings demonstrate that the crowdsourcing algorithm significantly outperforms the historical-data-only method, achieving a 20% reduction in total travel time.

Recent research indicates that flat-minima optimizers enhance neural network generalization by producing models with lower test errors. This study investigates the impact of flat-minima optimizers on the robustness of neural networks against adversarial attacks. We demonstrate that adversarial examples generated by such optimizers exhibit greater robustness compared to those trained with SGD. Specifically, adversarial samples targeting flat-minima optimizers require a higher number of iterations to converge and possess a larger optimal $\epsilon$ norm. These findings suggest that flat-minima optimizers offer a promising avenue for developing more robust neural networks.

This paper introduces a novel, compact, and low-cost reflective diode-based parametric frequency selective limiter (FSL) designed to mitigate electromagnetic interference (EMI) in wireless radios. The proposed limiter leverages the inherent nonlinearity of reflective diodes to generate a reflected signal that suppresses incoming interference. By utilizing a parametric approach, the device achieves high selectivity, effectively filtering out only specific interfering frequencies while leaving desired signals unimpacted. The study details the design and analysis of a prototype built using a reflective diode and a microstrip transmission line. Experimental results confirm that the prototype achieves an interference rejection ratio (IRR) of 20 dB and an insertion loss (IL) of 0.5 dB at the target frequency. Furthermore, the research explores the potential for miniaturizing the device by employing a coplanar waveguide (CPW) configuration.

This study introduces a stochastic model for infectious diseases that incorporates both the fundamental reproduction ratio and the effects of environmental noise. By utilizing the martingale central limit theorem, we establish the asymptotic normality of the number of infected individuals when the disease is endemic. Furthermore, we derive the expression for the variance of the limiting Gaussian distribution.

We introduce a straightforward yet effective method for generating vector representations of phrases by leveraging pre-trained word embeddings. This approach yields phrase vectors that are both semantically meaningful and capable of outperforming current state-of-the-art techniques on phrase similarity tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these phrase vectors can be effectively utilized for phrase clustering, achieving results that rival or exceed existing methods.

This study examines the count of $k$-order components in a random geometric graph, where vertices are distributed uniformly at random within a unit square and edges connect pairs whose distance does not exceed a threshold $r$. We demonstrate that, as $n$ approaches infinity, the variance of the number of $k$-order components is asymptotically equivalent to the square of its mean.

We introduce a novel Lagrangian framework for determining the equilibrium configurations of rotating stars, which incorporates a specific set of Lagrange multipliers to enforce the conservation of mass and momentum. This approach is designed to be compatible with any equation of state and remains applicable to both axisymmetric and triaxial stellar models. Furthermore, the method is formulated to be readily adaptable for use with finite element techniques.

This study examines the generalized Lema\^{i}tre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) spacetime, a spherically symmetric solution to Einstein's field equations that extends the standard LTB model. We analyze the properties of this generalized spacetime and contrast them with those of the conventional LTB model. Furthermore, we investigate the formation of a central singularity within the generalized framework, comparing these results to the singularity formation in standard LTB spacetime.

This approach involves taking the tensor product of two specific types of states: a bipartite set of locally irreducible states that is locally distinguishable, and a tripartite set of locally irreducible states that is locally indistinguishable. This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling web user behavior by integrating the concept of visit intention. We propose a new framework that incorporates this concept to enhance the precision of predicting user actions. Additionally, we develop a method for identifying visit intention and evaluate the proposed framework's performance using a real-world dataset.

This study introduces a transmissive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) designed to enhance communication performance in a multi-user scenario. The proposed RIS architecture features a dual-layer configuration where each layer is independently controlled by a specific set of phase shifters. The research investigates the joint optimization of transmit beamforming at the base station and the phase shifts for both RIS layers to maximize the minimum data rate across all users. The resulting optimization problem is non-convex and computationally demanding. To address this, we propose a low-complexity algorithm based on the Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method. The approach alternates between optimizing the transmit beamforming vectors and the phase shifts for both layers. The beamforming update is solved using a closed-form solution, while the phase shift update is addressed via a successive convex approximation technique. Theoretical analysis confirms that the algorithm converges to a stationary point. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing benchmarks in terms of computational efficiency and system performance.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) focuses on training policies using only static datasets, a scenario prevalent in fields like healthcare and robotics. While recent research has largely concentrated on mitigating distributional shifts between the data and the policy, this paper investigates a distinct challenge: the presence of unobserved confounders that influence both the data generation process and the reward function. We introduce a new framework for offline RL with unobserved confounders, which employs a latent variable model to represent these hidden factors. This approach utilizes a variational inference method to jointly optimize the policy and the latent variables. We demonstrate that our method achieves asymptotic optimality and validate its effectiveness through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This paper presents a novel framework for deriving free theorems regarding rank-2 and rank-3 polymorphic functions. By employing a category-theoretic approach, we establish a general method for constructing such free theorems applicable to any instance of a covariant functor within a functor category.

We report the discovery of a new galaxy, J0437+2456, which is the most distant object identified to date with a spectroscopically confirmed redshift. This galaxy was initially detected in the Subaru Deep Field (SDF) as a faint, red source with a magnitude of $i_{\rm AB} = 26.0$ and a color index of $(z-y)_{\rm AB} = 1.1$. Its redshift was determined to be $z = 10.4984 \pm 0.0003$ through spectroscopic analysis using the Subaru Hyper-Suprime-Cam (HSC) and the Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI). The measured recession velocity is $v_{\rm rec} = 14.9 \pm 0.1$ (stat) $\pm 0.2$ (sys) $\times 10^4$ km s$^{-1}$. This represents the highest redshift confirmed to date, surpassing the previous record holder, J0340+1300, by approximately 0.001 in redshift. The galaxy's spectral energy distribution (SED) is consistent with a stellar population age of roughly 300 Myr, with a metallicity of $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H}) \approx 7.5$. The galaxy's lumin

This paper examines the generalised syzygy problem within the three-body framework, focusing on the specific case of the equal-mass planar system. We present a numerical method to detect these syzygies and demonstrate that they are far more prevalent than previously believed.

Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful technique for characterizing the local environment of fluorophores, offering advantages over conventional imaging by providing information independent of fluorophore concentration. However, FLIM is often hindered by the need for extensive data acquisition and processing. To address this, we introduce a deep learning framework that enables rapid, high-quality FLIM reconstruction from a single snapshot. This approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on simulated data to predict fluorescence lifetimes from raw images. The model's accuracy was validated using both simulated datasets and real-world experiments involving a standard wide-field microscope. The results demonstrate that our method achieves high fidelity in FLIM reconstruction, with performance comparable to traditional techniques but at a significantly reduced acquisition time.

Personalized product search is a critical component of e-commerce, yet existing methods often fail to adequately model user preferences. This paper introduces a new framework for personalized search that integrates both user and product attributes, specifically focusing on the user's intent and the product's category. We propose a novel architecture utilizing a multi-modal, multi-task learning approach to jointly optimize relevance and click-through rate (CTR) prediction. This design enables the model to leverage the shared information between relevance and CTR tasks, thereby enhancing overall performance. Additionally, we employ a multi-modal strategy to fuse various input features, which improves the system's ability to capture complex user preferences. Experimental results on a real-world e-commerce dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a novel framework for graph embedding that leverages the inherent stability of the data. By employing a self-supervised approach, we generate auxiliary tasks to enhance the stability of learned representations. Specifically, we propose a new task designed to capture the local structural properties of the graph. Furthermore, we develop a meta-learning strategy to integrate these self-supervised tasks with the primary objective, thereby improving the robustness of the embeddings. Empirical results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques across various graph embedding applications.

Grant-free access is a promising solution for massive machine-type communications, enabling devices to transmit data without prior scheduling. This paper introduces a new multi-user detection framework for grant-free access that leverages a Bayesian approach to jointly estimate channel parameters and user activity. The proposed method is designed to handle multi-user interference and mitigate the effects of channel uncertainty. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the detection performance of this new framework is superior to that of existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a novel compressed sensing framework that utilizes a sparse coding matrix to generate a dictionary for signal reconstruction. By leveraging the sparsity inherent in the coding matrix, the proposed method constructs a dictionary that is both sparse and overcomplete. This approach is evaluated against the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction accuracy.

Random data augmentation is a prevalent technique for enhancing the generalization capabilities of deep neural networks. This study demonstrates that random augmentation can be effectively utilized to address domain adaptation challenges. We introduce a straightforward yet effective method for domain adaptation that employs a random augmentation strategy to generate synthetic training samples. This approach eliminates the need for any domain-specific knowledge or pre-training, while also avoiding the necessity of estimating domain discrepancy metrics. Experimental results across multiple datasets indicate that our method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches.

This paper examines the properties of 2-local inner derivations within the Jordan ring of self-adjoint matrices, $H_n(\mathbb{C})$, and establishes that every such derivation is necessarily a derivation. Additionally, we demonstrate that for $n \geq 3$, any 2-local derivation on the Jordan algebra of $n \times n$ self-adjoint matrices in a Hilbert space, $\mathcal{B}(H)^{op}$, is also a 2-local Jordan $*$-homomorphism. Furthermore, we show that for $n \geq 3$, every 2-local Jordan $*$-homomorphism on $\mathcal{B}(H)^{op}$ is in fact a Jordan $*$-homomorphism.

This study examines the adiabatic evolution of a two-level system, where the Hamiltonian's eigenstates and eigenvalues are derived analytically. By employing the instantaneous eigenstates, we calculate the Berry phase and the geometric phase within the context of the Aharonov-Anandan (AA) framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the AA phase can be expressed as a function of the Hamiltonian's parameters.

This study examines the existence and stability of compact matter waves within a binary Bose-Einstein condensate mixture, accounting for both inter- and intra-species nonlinearities alongside nonlocal interactions. We demonstrate that the system's nonlocal nature permits the formation of compact waves, which are characterized by a singular support and a vanishing gradient at the boundaries. The existence of these waves is contingent upon the specific values of the nonlinear and nonlocal parameters. Furthermore, we establish that such compact waves are inherently unstable.

We investigate the $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ and $D_{s1}(2536)$ resonances within the framework of the $D\bar{K}$ and $D^*\bar{K}$ systems, respectively, utilizing a non-relativistic quark model. Our analysis employs a separable potential characterized by a Gaussian form factor, with the interaction strength determined by the heavy-quark spin symmetry (HQSS) constraint. We demonstrate that the $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ and $D_{s1}(2536)$ can be interpreted as $D\bar{K}$ and $D^*\bar{K}$ bound states, respectively, and we calculate their decay widths into $D\pi$ and $D^*\pi$ channels.

This paper demonstrates that any continuous function defined on a compact set within the space of distributions can be approximated by smooth functions, provided the product of the corresponding Fourier transforms is integrable.

This study examines the production of an axion-like particle (ALP) in association with a Standard Model gauge boson, where the ALP subsequently decays into a pair of photons. We analyze the resulting phenomenology at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the future electron-positron collider, the International Linear Collider (ILC).

This paper introduces a hardware-software cooperative approach designed to enhance general-purpose processor performance by utilizing the processor's inherent capabilities. The proposed method involves a specialized hardware unit that offloads specific tasks to the processor, thereby reducing the processor's workload and improving overall system efficiency. The hardware-software interface is designed to be simple and intuitive, allowing for easy integration with existing systems. The paper also presents experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in various scenarios.

Deep networks trained on extensive image datasets have become a cornerstone of modern computer vision, yet their application to medical imaging remains limited due to the scarcity of labeled data. This paper introduces a new approach for training deep networks on medical images by leveraging pre-trained models from natural image domains. We demonstrate that initializing networks with weights from ImageNet significantly enhances performance on medical tasks, even with minimal data. This strategy is particularly effective for medical image segmentation, where we achieve state-of-the-art results on the 2D liver segmentation task using the LiTS dataset. Furthermore, we show that pre-training enables the training of compact models that rival the performance of larger architectures.

This study examines a singular quasi-linear elliptic system featuring a nonlocal term, establishing the existence of solutions via the sub- and supersolution method, while also exploring the related uniqueness issue.

Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are widely utilized for modeling sequential data, yet they often struggle to capture long-term dependencies due to the vanishing or exploding gradient problem. While recent advancements in RNN architectures have achieved significant success, this paper introduces a novel approach to training RNNs by leveraging the concept of "time" as a variable. We propose a new framework called Time-Dependent RNNs (TD-RNNs), which incorporates a time-dependent mechanism to enhance the modeling of long-term dependencies. Our method is evaluated on two benchmark datasets: the Penn Treebank corpus and the Google Speech Commands dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed TD-RNNs outperform existing state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) that are defined by a finite state space and a continuous action space. The proposed method relies on a Markov chain featuring a discrete state space and a continuous action space, which is proven to be ergodic under specific conditions. The algorithm's convergence is demonstrated, and numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate its performance.

We introduce a novel method for creating ultrashort, highly polarized electron bunches with attosecond precision. This approach utilizes a laser-driven, transverse electron accelerator to produce a beam of polarized positrons, which subsequently annihilates with electrons within the accelerator's cavity. This annihilation process yields an ultrabrilliant polarized attosecond electron bunch. The resulting beam exhibits a transverse size of approximately 100 nm and a longitudinal duration of roughly 100 fs. The proposed technique is compatible with existing electron accelerators and offers a pathway to generate polarized positrons with unprecedented brightness.

This study introduces a novel approach to the vital scalar field, a concept originally proposed by the author in 1999 to explain the growth of complexity in living organisms. The paper outlines the fundamental principles of this field and demonstrates its application to the human body, specifically focusing on the vital organs.

The European Commission's Horizon 2020 framework mandates that research outputs be made openly accessible to facilitate evidence-based policy-making within Science, Technology, and Innovation. To meet this requirement, the Commission has established a mandatory Open Access policy for all its programs, which includes a specific mandate for the reuse of data. This initiative is supported by the development of a comprehensive, open, and interoperable infrastructure designed to enable the discovery, access, and reuse of data generated under Horizon 2020. This paper outlines the current status of that data infrastructure and examines the key challenges involved in its implementation.

Smartphones are increasingly targeted by attackers exploiting side-channel vulnerabilities, which are security flaws that expose sensitive data through unintended system behaviors. This paper introduces a new side-channel detection framework designed to identify such vulnerabilities in Android applications. The system utilizes a hybrid approach combining static and dynamic analysis to pinpoint potential issues. The static analysis phase employs a data-flow analysis to locate sensitive variables, while the dynamic analysis phase leverages a user behavior model to identify side-channel events. The framework was evaluated against a dataset of 1,000 Android apps, revealing the detection of 1,000 side-channel vulnerabilities. The results indicate that the proposed framework is effective in identifying these security risks.

This study examines Ethereum account transaction patterns by analyzing the network structure of Ethereum accounts. We introduce a novel method for identifying communities within the Ethereum network and categorize these groups based on their network features. Our findings reveal that distinct account types exhibit unique transaction behaviors, which are reflected in the specific network features of their respective communities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Ethereum network's community structure remains stable over time, indicating that the underlying community organization is consistent across different periods.

We have measured the sheet resistance of a two-dimensional electron system at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface under varying illumination conditions. The observed changes in resistance are attributed to the generation of electron-hole pairs within the electron system. The resulting data aligns with a model assuming a constant photo-generation rate and a lifetime for these pairs that is independent of their density.

This paper examines the BV logic, which extends BCK logic with the axiom $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x \vee y$. We demonstrate that determining provability within BV is PSPACE-complete. Furthermore, we establish that the logic is not super-tautological, meaning there is no tautological upper bound for its provability strength.

We present a pentagon identity involving the quantum dilogarithm on the complex upper half-plane, expressed as a product formula for the corresponding zeta function. This result is derived by applying the functional equation of the zeta function to a specific functional relation for the quantum dilogarithm, which itself stems from the pentagon identity established by Faddeev.

We introduce a novel method for estimating photometric redshifts (photo-z) that leverages the capabilities of deep learning. This approach utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to process the photometric data of galaxies, specifically employing the 10-band photometry from the Dark Energy Survey (DES). Our training set comprises 1.5 million galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts drawn from the 3D-HST catalog. We evaluate our method's performance using the DES Science Verification (SV) catalog, which contains 1.1 million galaxies with photo-z estimates. Our results indicate that the median absolute error for the SV catalog is 0.003, with 90% of galaxies falling within an error range of 0.01. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our method surpasses the SV photo-z estimates in 80% of cases.

Gaussian Process (GP) emulators are widely used to approximate complex computer models, yet their effectiveness diminishes when the number of input variables is large. This study introduces a novel GP emulator that combines a sparse GP with a deep neural network (DNN) to address this challenge. The proposed method, termed the Sparse Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP), utilizes a DNN to model the relationship between inputs and the associated GP hyperparameters. By doing so, it enables the creation of a sparse GP emulator that is both computationally efficient and capable of handling high-dimensional inputs. The paper details the SNGP's architecture, training methodology, and theoretical underpinnings, alongside a demonstration of its application to a high-dimensional function approximation task.

We introduce QC-DMRG, a quantum computing approach that combines the strengths of DMRG and VQE to achieve high accuracy in two-electron systems using a bond dimension of 4. This method is designed to be adaptable for multi-electron systems, with a specific focus on the hydrogen molecule. By utilizing a single-qubit encoding scheme, QC-DMRG achieves a linear scaling of qubits relative to the system size. Furthermore, the method is capable of handling both Hermitian and non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

We introduce a straightforward extension of the Standard Model featuring a new non-Abelian gauge symmetry, $SU(2)_X$, which incorporates a new vector-like fermion doublet. This framework offers a viable explanation for the muon anomalous magnetic moment discrepancy. The model is capable of addressing the observed anomalies while remaining consistent with existing experimental constraints.

This study introduces a new framework for creating surrogate models of coastal and ocean systems, leveraging machine learning to capture the intricate, non-linear dynamics of these systems. The approach utilizes a deep neural network trained on data generated by a high-fidelity model, specifically the MITgcm, to approximate the response of a system to various forcing conditions. The paper demonstrates the method's efficacy by training the network to emulate the MITgcm's reaction to a suite of forcing scenarios, including a realistic representation of the 1997 El Niño event. The resulting surrogate model achieves high accuracy, with errors in the predicted sea surface height and temperature remaining below 10% of their respective standard deviations. The authors argue that this methodology holds significant promise for developing efficient, data-driven surrogates of climate models, which will be essential for addressing the computational challenges posed by climate change.

We introduce a publicly accessible, end-to-end analysis pipeline designed for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. This tool facilitates the creation of maps and power spectra from raw data, enabling researchers to assess the impact of various analysis choices and to benchmark their own methodologies. The software is built on a modular framework that allows for the seamless integration of new components. It is designed to be compatible with data from both single-dish and interferometric CMB instruments. The pipeline has been validated using simulated data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and the South Pole Telescope (SPT), as well as with actual data from the ACT.

This study examines Turing instability within a reaction-diffusion framework featuring a non-local term, specifically a non-local reaction component. We demonstrate that this non-local reaction can induce Turing instability even when the standard local reaction is stable. Furthermore, we establish that the system can exhibit both stationary and oscillatory Turing instabilities.

We examine a deformation of pure Yang-Mills theory driven by a phantom field, a non-unitary scalar that possesses a negative kinetic term. This modification generates a new interaction between the phantom and the gluons, which precisely offsets the quantum corrections arising from the phantom's own loops. Consequently, the theory remains finite at the one-loop level, mirroring the ultraviolet finiteness of N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. This result is derived using the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, which ensures the deformation maintains gauge invariance.

We investigated the polarization characteristics of photoluminescence in GaAs/AlGaAs nanowires, specifically examining the influence of nanowire orientation and the polarization state of the excitation laser. Our findings indicate that the polarization behavior is governed by the alignment between the nanowire axis and the crystallographic c-axis of the substrate.

This study addresses the challenge of inferring an opponent's priorities within multi-issue negotiation. We introduce a novel approach that utilizes a Bayesian network to model the opponent's utility function, thereby enabling the prediction of their issue-based preferences. We evaluate this method against a baseline that relies on a fixed, pre-defined utility function. Experimental results indicate that our proposed technique outperforms the baseline, achieving superior outcomes in both the quantity of agreements reached and the total utility generated.

This study examines the dynamics of a fundamental string within a braneworld framework featuring a dynamical string tension. We demonstrate that the string's motion is governed by a modified Dirac action, where the tension is treated as a dynamical variable. This approach yields a specific Lagrangian for the string's worldsheet, which incorporates a potential term dependent on the string's length. We analyze the resulting equations of motion and show that the string's dynamics are equivalent to those of a point particle moving in a potential. Furthermore, we investigate the implications of this model for the confinement of strings and matter in braneworld scenarios.

This paper introduces a new method for online field experiments that balances covariate information across treatment groups. The approach is grounded in a sequential randomization framework, where the probability of assigning a unit to a specific treatment is determined by the current balance of covariate data. The method's performance is evaluated using both simulated datasets and a real-world application involving a randomized trial of a job training program.

This study presents a first-principles investigation into the (001)-Si/(001)-$\gamma$-Al$_2$O$_3$ heterointerface, which is crucial for the development of Si-based high-temperature electronics. We demonstrate that all interfacial Si atoms maintain fourfold coordination, while interfacial Al atoms adopt a distorted octahedral structure. The interface is characterized by a 0.45 eV band offset, with the valence band maximum situated at the $\Gamma$ point and the conduction band minimum located at the X point. Furthermore, the interface exhibits a robust covalent bond between Si and Al atoms, accompanied by a significant charge transfer from the Si layer to the $\gamma$-Al$_2$O$_3$ layer.
This study employs the numerical shooting method to estimate the functions associated with four-dimensional axion-dilaton black holes.

The shipping industry's container crisis was precipitated by a mismatch between the supply of containers and the demand for cargo, a situation that has since been exacerbated by the pandemic. This paper introduces a novel framework for forecasting container supply and demand, utilizing a deep learning model that integrates both historical time-series data and current news events. The study evaluates the model's performance across three distinct datasets, demonstrating its efficacy in predicting the dynamics of the container crisis.

This study introduces a novel approach to streaming anomaly detection that leverages the concept of data sparsity. The proposed method, named Sparse Anomaly Detector (SAD), utilizes a sparse representation framework to identify anomalies within the data stream. SAD is designed to be computationally efficient, capable of processing new data points in real-time with minimal latency. The paper further details the theoretical underpinnings of SAD, specifically addressing its sensitivity to the sparsity of normal data and the influence of the dictionary's size. Additionally, the authors evaluate SAD's performance against various existing anomaly detection techniques across multiple datasets. The results demonstrate that SAD achieves superior performance compared to competing methods, particularly in scenarios involving sparse normal data.

Glioma segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging that supports diagnosis and treatment planning. While recent deep learning models have achieved high accuracy, they often overlook essential substructures like the tumor core and edema, which are vital for determining prognosis and guiding therapy. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that integrates a multi-scale encoder with a multi-branch decoder to simultaneously segment the whole tumor and its key substructures. This approach utilizes a multi-scale encoder to capture diverse contextual details and employs a multi-branch decoder to isolate specific substructures, thereby enhancing segmentation precision. Furthermore, we incorporate a novel attention mechanism to refine feature representation and boost overall performance. Experimental results on the BraTS 2021 dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving Dice scores of 90.1%, 89.1%, 84.1%, and 97.1% for the whole tumor, tumor core, enhancing tumor, and edema, respectively.

This study examines the triplon, a spin-1 excitation found in quantum antiferromagnets with frustrated interactions. We introduce a new method for calculating triplon dispersion relations in these systems, utilizing a spin-1 Green's function derived from a bosonic representation of the Hubbard model. This approach is validated by comparing our results with exact diagonalization data for a square lattice. Furthermore, we analyze the triplon dispersion in a triangular lattice, focusing on the regime of weak frustration. We identify a distinct triplon band that emerges from the Mott insulator state when frustration is introduced.

This paper introduces the concept of statistical convergence based on asymptotic density using an arbitrary admissible filter. It further explores the relationship between this new form of statistical convergence and traditional statistical convergence defined by natural density.

This study introduces a novel discontinuous Galerkin finite element method for solving the time-fractional subdiffusion equation. We establish optimal error estimates for both the semi-discrete and fully discrete formulations. Additionally, we derive an optimal error bound for the fully discrete scheme under the assumption of temporal smoothness. Numerical experiments are included to validate the theoretical findings.

This paper examines a coupled system of partial differential equations that models the interaction between a fluid and a solid body. The analysis focuses on the well-posedness of the problem, utilizing the Babuška-Brezzi Theorem, and further investigates the existence of a weak solution to the corresponding time-discrete scheme.

We have theoretically investigated the optical selection rules governing charged interlayer excitons in a bilayer system subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. Our analysis reveals that the magnetic field induces a transition from a circular to a linear polarization regime, a phenomenon driven by the interplay between the Zeeman effect and the magnetic-field-driven cyclotron motion.

This study introduces the inaugural results from the 10-meter GTC telescope's high-resolution spectroscopic campaign, utilizing the UVES instrument to observe the globular cluster NGC 6397. The primary objective is to determine the radial velocities of approximately 1,000 cluster members, with a precision better than 0.5 km/s, to facilitate the identification of potential exoplanet hosts. The analysis of the data reveals a mean radial velocity of -100.7 ± 0.1 km/s, with a dispersion of 10.6 km/s. The derived velocity dispersion aligns with the cluster's dynamical model, while the mean velocity matches the expected value for the cluster's systemic motion. This study introduces a new deep neural network architecture designed to address inverse scattering problems. By utilizing a deep neural network, we can efficiently and accurately solve these problems, surpassing the performance of traditional optimization techniques. The proposed method is trained on a dataset comprising numerous forward scattering simulations, which are generated using a deep neural network that models the forward scattering process. Accelerated degradation testing (ADT) is a vital tool in reliability engineering for forecasting the remaining useful life of a product. This study introduces a novel Bayesian ADT framework that integrates multiple stress levels and incorporates a random effect to account for unit-to-unit variability. The proposed model utilizes a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to estimate parameters, with the efficacy of the inference method validated through a simulation study. Furthermore, the model is applied to analyze data from a battery ADT experiment.

This study examines the centrality dependence of triangular flow ($v_3$) in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76$ TeV, utilizing the ALICE detector. The $v_3$ is derived from the three-particle cumulant method, with the third-order event plane resolution ($\Psi_3$) calculated via the three-particle correlation technique. The analysis covers centralities ranging from 0% to 80% and includes both positive and negative $v_3$ values. The resulting $v_3$ values are compared against hydrodynamic model predictions, which demonstrate strong agreement with the experimental data.

This study examines the thermodynamic characteristics of an Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection (ICME) detected by STEREO-A on 2014 May 12. Utilizing in-situ data from the WIND spacecraft, we analyzed the ICME's thermodynamic evolution, specifically focusing on its entropy and temperature. Our findings indicate that the ICME's entropy remained nearly constant, with a polytropic index of 1.01, suggesting an isothermal process. Furthermore, the ICME's temperature was found to be governed by the ambient solar wind temperature.

This paper examines the Random Waypoint Mobility Model (RWPM) for Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks (MANETs), a framework where nodes move randomly within a bounded region. We demonstrate that the Birkhoff pointwise ergodic theorem applies to this model, establishing the existence of a unique stationary distribution for the system. Furthermore, we derive the probability density function for the inter-node distance under this stationary condition.

This study examines the impact of Coulomb final-state interactions on $K^+K^-$ pair production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV. Data were collected using the BESIII detector at the BEPCII accelerator, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 1.07 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis focuses on the $K^+K^-$ invariant mass spectrum, specifically within the range of 100 to 1000 MeV$/c^2$, and investigates the dependence of the $K^+K^-$ yield on the longitudinal momentum of the kaons. The results indicate that Coulomb interactions enhance the $K^+K^-$ yield at low longitudinal momenta, with the effect diminishing as momentum increases.

The microscopic calculation of collective inertial mass coefficients for the $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O reaction is performed using the energy-dependent quasiparticle random-phase approximation (QRPA). This approach employs the energy-dependent mass coefficient tensor, which is derived from the imaginary component of the energy-dependent optical potential via the optical theorem. The resulting mass coefficients are then utilized to solve the collective Schrödinger equation, yielding the collective wave function. Finally, the total cross section is determined by integrating the product of the collective wave function and the relative kinetic energy.

The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) has emerged as a prominent benchmark for assessing artificial intelligence algorithms, with its primary objective being the derivation of a rule that maps an input grid to a corresponding output grid. While previous research has predominantly concentrated on the neural network architecture, this study introduces a novel approach that utilizes a graph-based method to solve ARC tasks. We demonstrate that this graph-driven strategy achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art neural models.

This study examines the regularity of entropy solutions for scalar conservation laws featuring discontinuous fluxes. We establish that, for fluxes that are Lipschitz continuous, entropy solutions belong to a fractional BV space with a specific exponent. This exponent is determined by the smallest value of the derivative of the flux across all its discontinuity points. Furthermore, we demonstrate that solutions to the associated vanishing viscosity problem converge to entropy solutions within a fractional BV space, with a rate of convergence defined by a specific exponent. This convergence exponent is derived from the minimum of the derivative of the flux at discontinuity points and the exponent characterizing the regularity of the flux's discontinuities.

This study reports the first observation of the doubly Cabibbo-suppressed decay $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-}\pi^{+}$, utilizing a dataset of $3.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of $7$ and $8\,\text{TeV}$. The branching fraction ratio relative to the doubly Cabibbo-favored mode, $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-}K^{+}$, is determined to be $R_{\text{DCS}} = \mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-}\pi^{+})/\mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-}K^{+}) = (0.020 \pm 0.004\text{(stat)} \pm 0.003\text{(syst)})$. This result aligns with theoretical predictions, and the measured ratio is consistent with the previously observed value for the related $D^{0}\pi^{+}/D^{-}K^{+}$ ratio.

This study introduces a novel approach to enhance spectral efficiency in distributed massive MIMO systems by enabling concurrent data transmission through the use of superposition coding. The proposed method employs a successive interference cancellation (SIC) scheme at the base station, where signals from multiple users are superimposed and decoded sequentially. The work derives the achievable rate region for this framework and formulates a joint optimization problem aimed at maximizing the minimum user rate. The solution involves a two-stage algorithm: first, a power allocation strategy is developed to maximize the minimum user rate under a fixed power splitting ratio, followed by a power splitting optimization to maximize the minimum user rate given fixed power levels. The efficacy of this approach is validated through numerical simulations.

The shuffle model of differential privacy (DP) has recently gained significant attention for its ability to balance privacy and utility better than purely local mechanisms. This paper introduces a new shuffle model that leverages the privacy amplification inherent in shuffling. Our approach achieves a privacy-utility trade-off that surpasses the best existing results for shuffle-based DP. Specifically, we demonstrate that our method matches the performance of the central DP model when using Gaussian mechanisms, while also providing a more efficient analysis for Laplacian mechanisms.

Orthogonal time frequency multiplexing (OTFS) has recently emerged as a promising candidate for future wireless communication systems, offering superior performance compared to orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in high-mobility environments. This paper introduces Orthogonal Time Sequency Modulation (OTSM), a new modulation scheme that shares the same fundamental principles as OTFS but operates within a distinct signal space. By utilizing the Fourier transform instead of the inverse Fourier transform for signal transmission, OTSM achieves a more efficient use of the frequency domain. Additionally, the study presents a new modulation technique called Orthogonal Time Sequency Code Division Multiplexing (OTSCDM), which extends the concept of orthogonal time-sequency code-division multiple access (OTSCDMA) to the frequency domain. This new scheme offers improved spectral efficiency and reduced computational complexity compared to existing methods.

This paper investigates the existence of a faithful irreducible representation for a right cancellative semigroup $S$ equipped with a weight $w$ that fulfills the F-property, defined as $w(s+st) = w(t+st)$ for all $s,t \in S$. We demonstrate that such a faithful irreducible representation exists if and only if $S$ is left cancellative and $w$ adheres to the condition $w(s+t) = w(t)$ for all $s,t \in S$.

This study investigates the fluid dynamics of a molten metal melt pool, accounting for surface tension gradients, buoyancy, and electromagnetic forces. The analysis utilizes a two-dimensional axisymmetric model, where the flow is driven by an absorbed energy flux that varies with the radial distance from the center. The governing equations are solved via a finite element method, with the energy equation solved concurrently to determine the melt pool's temperature field. The resulting flow behavior is examined across different melt pool geometries and varying electromagnetic parameters. The findings indicate that the flow remains laminar under all tested conditions. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the flow's characteristics are highly sensitive to the specific form of the energy flux distribution.

The future of public transportation will likely feature wireless charging capabilities, allowing passengers to power their devices during transit. This study examines the security of such systems, specifically focusing on the risks posed by malicious actors who could intercept wireless signals to steal data from user devices. We introduce a novel attack model that exploits the inherent physical characteristics of the wireless charging environment to compromise the confidentiality of the communication channel. Our approach involves a new method for extracting sensitive information from a victim's device by leveraging the unique properties of the wireless charging setup. We have developed a prototype system to validate the feasibility of this attack, demonstrating that it can successfully retrieve data from a victim's device. Our findings indicate that the proposed attack is effective and poses a significant threat to the security of future wireless charging systems.

We demonstrate that for any Boolean function $f$ defined on $\{0,1\}^n$, there exists a real polynomial $P$ of degree $d$ such that $|P(x) - f(x)| \leq 1/2$ for all $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, where $d$ is the smallest possible degree satisfying this pointwise approximation requirement. This result is achieved by constructing $P$ as a multivariate polynomial of degree $d$ over the reals, with coefficients determined by a specific optimization process involving the function $f$. The proof relies on a novel application of the probabilistic method, combined with a careful analysis of the behavior of the function $f$ on the hypercube.

This study examines the bistability within dynamical systems, specifically focusing on the coexistence of two attractors. We categorize these bistable structures into two types: those involving two basins of attraction and those involving one basin and one basin boundary. We demonstrate that the latter type can be modeled as a one-dimensional system. Furthermore, we show that the coexistence of two attractors in one-dimensional systems is a universal feature, occurring in any one-dimensional system with a non-zero Lyapunov exponent. We also provide a method for calculating the probability of transitioning between two attractors in one-dimensional systems. Finally, we show that the probability of transitioning between two attractors in one-dimensional systems is a universal feature, occurring in any one-dimensional system with a non-zero Lyapunov exponent.
